narrative: Today's strongest signal is climate-driven range dynamics: two Ecography studies show that range shifts often lag realised climate change, disguising continued climatic sensitivity, while a third finds microhabitat variability can override macroclimatic suitability in predicting where species actually establish. Fire ecology contributes a Global Change Biology finding that post-fire recovery trajectories in temperate vegetation depend on the interaction between fire severity and hydro-climatic moisture conditions, complementing a remote-sensing characterisation of post-fire forest composition shifts across boreal Eastern Siberia. Several papers extend understanding of trophic complexity and stability: a new superposition method streamlines food-web reconstruction from stable isotope data, while nutrient enrichment is shown to destabilise multi-trophic food webs by synchronising dynamics within and across trophic levels. Behavioural ecology work in Journal of Animal Ecology highlights social behaviour as an underappreciated buffer against environmental change, alongside evidence that spatial and social phenotypes co-vary in an avian scavenger. On invasion and symbiosis, biological invasions are shown to reorganise the environmental axes structuring niches rather than simply shifting them, and mycorrhizal partnerships emerge repeatedly as mediators of both nutrient acquisition and competitive outcomes between native and invasive plants. In conservation and landscape ecology, two decades of tropical forest restoration monitoring in Costa Rica shows planted-tree treatments accumulate far more biomass than natural regeneration, while community-managed forests in Indonesia demonstrate that habitat connectivity is central to sustaining biodiversity outcomes. Methodological advances are notable this cycle, including a zero-shot bioacoustic classifier for frog calls, an open-source real-time animal re-identification tool for edge devices, and a new edge-computing acoustic-monitoring prototype built for citizen science at continental scale.
